title: BECE Basic Science - Basic Science - The Environment
subject: Basic Science

questions.q: Which of the following defines environmental pollution?
options: The planting of trees in an environment
The release of harmful substances into the environment
questions.explain: Pollution is the introduction of harmful materials (pollutants) into the environment.
questions.subject: Basic Science

questions.q: Which gas is primarily responsible for global warming?
questions.explain: Carbon dioxide is a major greenhouse gas that traps heat in the atmosphere, contributing to global warming.
questions.subject: Basic Science

questions.q: Water pollution can lead to the spread of which of the following diseases?
questions.explain: Cholera is a waterborne disease caused by ingesting water contaminated with bacteria.
questions.subject: Basic Science

questions.q: Anything that has mass and occupies space is known as:
questions.explain: Matter is defined as anything that has mass and takes up space (volume).
questions.subject: Basic Science

questions.q: Which of the following is a characteristic of all living things?
questions.explain: Excretion is one of the characteristics of living things (MR NIGER D), whereas flying, having leaves, or fur are specific to only some organisms.
questions.subject: Basic Science

questions.q: The process by which a solid changes directly to a gas without passing through the liquid state is called:
questions.explain: Sublimation is the transition of a substance directly from the solid to the gas state.
questions.subject: Basic Science

questions.q: Which of these materials is non-biodegradable?
questions.explain: Polythene (plastic) does not decompose easily by biological processes, unlike organic materials like paper, fruit peels, or wood.
questions.subject: Basic Science

questions.q: The boiling point of pure water at sea level is:
questions.explain: Pure water boils at 100 degrees Celsius under standard atmospheric pressure.
questions.subject: Basic Science

questions.q: Which method is best for separating a mixture of sand and water?
questions.explain: Filtration allows the liquid (water) to pass through while trapping the insoluble solid (sand).
questions.subject: Basic Science

questions.q: In the acronym MR NIGER D representing the characteristics of living things, what does 'R' stand for?
questions.explain: R stands for Respiration (or Reproduction in some variations, but Respiration is the standard primary 'R').
questions.subject: Basic Science

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a state of matter?
questions.explain: Solid, Liquid, and Gas are states of matter. Energy is not a state of matter.
questions.subject: Basic Science

questions.q: The basic unit of life in organisms is the:
questions.explain: The cell is the fundamental structural and functional unit of all living organisms.
questions.subject: Basic Science

questions.q: Plants remove carbon dioxide from the air during:
questions.explain: During photosynthesis, plants take in carbon dioxide and water to produce glucose and oxygen.
questions.subject: Basic Science

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of an inorganic (non-living) matter found in the soil?
questions.explain: Sand particles are mineral components derived from rocks (inorganic). Humus, bacteria, and earthworms are organic or living components.
questions.subject: Basic Science

questions.q: Proper disposal of refuse and sewage helps to prevent:
questions.explain: Waste management prevents pollution of land and water bodies.
questions.subject: Basic Science

questions.q: Acid rain is primarily caused by the release of which gases?
questions.explain: Sulphur dioxide ($SO_2$) and Nitrogen oxides ($NO_x$) react with water vapor to form acid rain.
questions.subject: Basic Science

questions.q: The quantity of matter contained in a body is called its:
questions.explain: Mass is defined as the amount of matter in an object, whereas weight is the force of gravity on that mass.
questions.subject: Basic Science

questions.q: Which of the following is a renewable natural resource?
questions.explain: Solar energy is renewable because it is naturally replenished. Fossil fuels like crude oil, coal, and natural gas are non-renewable.
questions.subject: Basic Science
